note: Maintained daily. Every item links to the page that confirms it.

happened.title: CNN polls: El-Sayed +7 in Michigan, Talarico +6 in Texas, Jackson +4 in Maine, Hamilton +4 in Kansas
happened.what: CNN polls by SSRS of likely voters (Oct 20-27) have Abdul El-Sayed 49-42 over Mike Rogers in Michigan and James Talarico 49-43 over Ken Paxton in Texas; in Oct 20-26 surveys, Troy Jackson leads Susan Collins 49-45 in Maine and Adam Hamilton leads Sen. Roger Marshall 49-45 in Kansas, where Hamilton draws about 12% of Republicans. Collins' unfavorable rating is 54%; the Texas governor race had no clear leader.
happened.why: Democrats leading in all four, including two Republican-held seats Cook rates Toss Up, is the path to a Senate majority; at least one in eight likely voters in every state but Maine said they could still switch.
happened.src: CNN (Jennifer Agiesta, Ariel Edwards-Levy and Jennifer Wu), Oct 29

happened.title: Alaska: Times reports a Peltola-linked operative recruited the second 'Dan Sullivan'; Trump demands prosecution, Dunleavy orders a state probe
happened.what: A New York Times report said a Democratic operative who worked with Mary Peltola's campaign and national Democrats helped encourage retired teacher Daniel J. Sullivan Jr. to run against Sen. Dan Sullivan; Peltola's campaign said it 'has no involvement with either Sullivan campaign' and the DSCC said it 'is not involved.' Trump wrote that Peltola should not 'be allowed to run' and 'should be prosecuted,' and on Thursday called for both to be removed from the ballot; Gov. Mike Dunleavy directed the Department of Public Safety to investigate. U.S. District Judge Sharon Gleason let Peltola's campaign, the DSCC and voting-rights groups intervene in the Justice Department's certification suit, where DOJ now seeks expedited discovery from the Peltola campaign and a dismissal ruling could come this week.
happened.why: Alaska is one of the Democrats' five likeliest pickups, and the ballot-stacking story and DOJ suit now hang over the final week and the count.
happened.src: CBS News (Joe Walsh), Oct 28; PBS NewsHour/AP (Becky Bohrer and Nicholas Riccardi), Oct 28; HuffPost via Yahoo, Oct 29; Washington Sun/NOTUS (Adora Brown), Oct 28

happened.title: Judge Carter refuses to segregate 20,000 California mail ballots; DOJ appeals to the 9th Circuit
happened.what: In a 26-page order, U.S. District Judge David O. Carter denied the Justice Department's request for a temporary restraining order that would have made California set aside about 20,000 mail ballots from voters the administration called likely noncitizens, writing that the relief would 'wreak havoc' on the midterms and that voters should not lose a core right 'merely because of unfounded allegations.' First Assistant U.S. Attorney Bill Essayli said DOJ filed an immediate appeal Wednesday evening with the Solicitor General's approval; the 9th Circuit had dismissed an earlier DOJ appeal 2-1 on Oct 26, and Carter had appointed a special master on Oct 27.
happened.why: The ruling leaves California's count untouched for now in three Toss Up House seats, with the appeal the remaining route to disrupt it before Election Day.
happened.src: ABC7 Los Angeles, Oct 29; California Post via Yahoo (Pierce Sharpe), Oct 28; CBS News (Melissa Quinn), Oct 26

happened.title: Final-week state polls: Marquette has Crowley +7 in Wisconsin; Mitchell, UMass Lowell and High Point give Democrats 7 to 14 points in Michigan, New Hampshire and North Carolina
happened.what: Marquette Law School's final Wisconsin poll (Oct 14-22) has David Crowley 51-44 over Tom Tiffany among likely voters, his largest lead of the cycle, with Trump at 37% approve, 61% disapprove in the state. Mitchell Research for CBS Detroit (Oct 26-27) has Abdul El-Sayed 51-44 over Mike Rogers; UMass Lowell (Oct 2-19) has Chris Pappas 48-41 over John E. Sununu and Kelly Ayotte 48-42 over Cinde Warmington; High Point University (Oct 1-20) has Roy Cooper 54-40 over Michael Whatley.
happened.why: The Republican-held Wisconsin governorship, Michigan's open Senate seat and North Carolina's Senate seat all look Democratic in the final independent polls.
happened.src: Marquette Law School, Oct 28; WPR (Rich Kremer), Oct 28; CBS Detroit, Oct 28; UMass Lowell, Oct 28; High Point University, Oct 28

happened.title: Obama rallies a packed arena in Morrow, Ga., for Ossoff and Bottoms
happened.what: Former President Barack Obama told a crowd at the Arena at SouthLake that the midterm is the 'last, best chance to rein in some of the foolishness,' saying Trump is 'virtually doing arts and crafts while we are fighting a war and trying to deal with out-of-control prices' and that 'these are not serious people.' Sen. Jon Ossoff called the administration 'the most corrupt administration in American history'; Keisha Lance Bottoms said 'Slick Rick is running to be Trump's favorite governor, and I'm running to be yours.' Sen. Raphael Warnock spoke and Janelle Monae performed.
happened.why: It opened a three-day Democratic surrogate push (Harris follows Thursday and Friday) in the final days of Georgia's early voting, with a Toss Up governor race on the ballot.
happened.src: Capital B Atlanta (Chauncey Alcorn), Oct 28; AP via Click2Houston (Mike Catalini), Oct 28; WSB-TV (Courtney Martinez), Oct 28

happened.title: Sununu criticizes Trump's Iran war and tariffs in the final New Hampshire Senate debate
happened.what: In the WMUR debate, John E. Sununu, Trump's endorsed candidate, criticized the president's handling of the Iran war and tariffs; Chris Pappas said Sununu had 'cheered it on from the beginning,' and the two clashed over Social Security, with Sununu calling Pappas' attack 'designed to scare senior citizens.' The NRSC's post-debate statement attacked 'Party Line Pappas' over tax votes and an undisclosed relationship with a lobbyist.
happened.why: New Hampshire is a Lean D open seat Democrats need to hold; Sununu is running against Trump's record in a state where polls have Pappas ahead by 6 to 7.
happened.src: CBS News live blog, Oct 29; NRSC statement, Oct 28

happened.title: Times/Siena: South Carolina Senate tied 48-48; Moody +6 in Florida, Flanagan +14 in Minnesota
happened.what: Siena's final-week polls of likely voters for The New York Times have Annie Andrews and Darline Graham tied 48-48 in South Carolina, with Alan Wilson leading the governor race 51-44; Ashley Moody 50-44 over Angie Nixon and Byron Donalds 48-44 over David Jolly in Florida; and Peggy Flanagan 54-40 over Michele Tafoya and Amy Klobuchar 56-38 in Minnesota.
happened.why: A tie in a Republican-held South Carolina seat widens the Democratic Senate map, while Florida and Minnesota look like holds for the incumbent parties.

happened.title: Suffolk: Brown 47-44 and Acton 48-44 in Ohio; Echelon has both Ohio races even
happened.what: Suffolk University/USA TODAY Network Ohio (Oct 21-26, 500 voters) has Sherrod Brown 47-44 over Jon Husted and Amy Acton 48-44 over Vivek Ramaswamy, unchanged from its Oct 2 Senate reading; Echelon Insights for NetChoice (Oct 16-23, 508 likely voters) has the Senate race 47-47 and Ramaswamy 47-45, with Ossoff 55-40 in Georgia, Turek 45-43 in Iowa, Ricketts 47-46 over Osborn in Nebraska, Jackson 51-44 in Maine and Moody 51-43 in Florida.
happened.why: Ohio's Senate seat is the Democrats' likeliest pickup, and the final-week polls keep it inside the margin of error.
happened.src: Suffolk University Political Research Center, Oct 28; NetChoice (Echelon Insights), Oct 27
happened.aff: Echelon Insights is a Republican-aligned pollster; NetChoice is a tech trade association

happened.title: Murkowski endorses Democrat Kreiss-Tomkins for Alaska governor
happened.what: Sen. Lisa Murkowski endorsed Democrat Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins over Trump-backed Republican Bernadette Wilson in the ranked-choice race for Alaska's open governorship.
happened.why: A cross-party endorsement from Alaska's senior senator in a Republican-held governorship that the raters already lean Democratic.
happened.src: Fox News live blog (Alex Nitzberg), Oct 28

happened.title: Sabato's Crystal Ball: North Carolina Senate to Likely D, South Carolina to Lean R; 225 House seats at least lean D
happened.what: Sabato's final-week update moves the open North Carolina Senate seat from Leans to Likely Democratic, South Carolina from Likely to Leans Republican and Florida from Safe to Likely Republican, leaving 49 seats at least leaning Democratic, 46 Republican and 5 toss-ups; in the House, PA-08 and TX-15 move to Leans Democratic and KY-06, MT-01, CO-05, MO-02, PA-01, VA-05 and AL-02 to Toss-up, for 225 seats at least leaning Democratic, 193 Republican and 17 toss-ups; Arizona's governor race moves to Likely Democratic and Vermont's to Leans Republican.
happened.why: The raters now have Democrats at a House majority without any toss-up and 'the inside track' to a narrow Senate majority of 51 or 52 seats.

happened.title: Cook's final governor ratings shift two states toward Democrats, project a 2-4 seat gain
happened.what: Cook Political Report's final governors ratings move two states toward Democrats and say 'Democrats are in a prime position to pick up between two and four governor's seats this cycle,' which would give them a majority of governorships for the first time since 2010; Cook's tracker puts Trump's approval at 36.4%.
happened.why: Democrats hold 24 governorships and need 26 for a majority; the raters now put that within reach.
happened.src: Cook Political Report (CPR In Brief), Oct 27

happened.title: SLF launches ads in eight Senate states and Mississippi; Democrats pull from North Carolina
happened.what: Senate Leadership Fund released new ads against Peltola, Turek, Hamilton, Jackson, El-Sayed, Osborn, Pappas and Brown and placed a low-seven-figure buy defending Cindy Hyde-Smith after Senate Majority PAC's $1.2 million Mississippi campaign; Legis1's Oct 21-22 filings tally had Democratic super PACs adding $6.7 million to Republicans' $4.1 million, with WinSenate adding $2.2 million in Ohio but cutting $525,000 in North Carolina and SLF withdrawing $239,000 in Georgia.
happened.why: Republican money defending a Solid R seat and Democrats trimming North Carolina show where each side thinks the map has moved.
happened.src: Senate Leadership Fund, Oct 23; Semafor (Burgess Everett), Oct 22; Legis1, Oct 22

happened.title: Cook shifts 19 House seats toward Democrats, projects a 12-22 seat gain
happened.what: Cook Political Report moved 19 House races toward Democrats, including six toss-ups to Lean Democrat (four of them Republican-held) and two open Republican seats to Toss Up, leaving 220 seats at least leaning Democratic, 198 Republican and 17 toss-ups (12 Republican-held), and projected a Democratic gain of 12 to 22 seats for a 227-237 seat majority.
happened.why: The raters' House range now sits at or above the model's seat count rather than below it.

upcoming.title: Maine no-excuse absentee voting period ends
upcoming.what: Oct. 29 is the last day of Maine's no-excuse absentee period, including in-person absentee voting at town and city halls.
upcoming.why: The deadline shapes early ballots in the Collins-Jackson Senate race and the ME-02 House race.

upcoming.title: Kentucky early in-person voting begins
upcoming.what: Kentucky's three days of no-excuse early in-person voting run Thursday, Oct. 29, through Saturday, Oct. 31.
upcoming.why: Early votes begin in the open KY-06, which Inside Elections moved to Tilt Republican on Oct. 20, and the Barr-Booker Senate race.

upcoming.title: Wisconsin mail absentee request deadline
upcoming.what: Requests for mailed absentee ballots are due to clerks by 5 p.m. CT; in-person absentee voting continues through about Nov 1, varying by municipality.
upcoming.why: Wisconsin's absentee returns have caught up with 2022, and the last days of in-person absentee voting through Nov 1 decide the final early total.

upcoming.title: Harris in Macon and Atlanta for Ossoff, Bottoms
upcoming.what: Former Vice President Kamala Harris opens a Democratic canvass launch in Macon (program 1:45 p.m.), then joins an NAACP community town hall with Derrick Johnson in Atlanta and a mobilization event with Sen. Jon Ossoff, the second day of a three-day Georgia visit.
upcoming.why: Democrats are stacking their biggest surrogates into Georgia's last two days of early voting, with a Toss Up governor race and Ossoff's seat on the ballot.
upcoming.src: 41NBC (Tucker Sargent), Oct 26; Atlanta News First (Tim Darnell), Oct 29

upcoming.title: Pingree, Russell debate in Maine's 1st District
upcoming.what: Maine Public hosts a debate between Rep. Chellie Pingree and Republican Ron Russell at 7 p.m. on its radio, television and streams.
upcoming.why: It is the only scheduled debate in a Democratic-held seat that becomes competitive only in a Republican year.

upcoming.title: Bresnahan, Cognetti debate on WVIA in PA-08
upcoming.what: Rep. Rob Bresnahan (R) and Scranton Mayor Paige Cognetti (D) debate for an hour at WVIA's Pittston studios, moderated by Tracey Matisak with a panel from WVIA News, the Citizens' Voice and PCN; on WVIA-TV, WVIA-FM, the WVIA app and WVIA News' YouTube channel, with a live post-debate show.
upcoming.why: Cook rates PA-08 a Toss Up and Inside Elections moved it to Tilt Democratic on Oct. 20; it is one of the Republican-held seats Democrats need for a majority.

upcoming.title: Georgia and Texas in-person early voting ends
upcoming.what: Friday, Oct. 30, is the last day of in-person early voting in Georgia and in Texas.
upcoming.why: The final early-vote totals in two Senate battlegrounds and the Georgia and Texas governor races set the Election Day math for both parties.
upcoming.src: Axios Atlanta, Oct 19; FOX 7 Austin, Oct 12

upcoming.title: Nevada in-person early voting ends
upcoming.what: Clark County's early-voting sites close after Oct 30 (some are closed that day for Nevada Day); mail ballots can still be returned through Election Day.
upcoming.why: Democrats lead Nevada's early vote by about 6 points, and Election Day's Republican turnout decides the governor race.
upcoming.src: Clark County Election Department notice, accessed Oct 26

upcoming.title: Harris headlines Fulton County Democrats fundraiser
upcoming.what: Harris closes her Georgia swing at a Fulton County Democratic Party fundraiser in Atlanta on the last day of in-person early voting.
upcoming.why: Fulton is the Democrats' largest vote source in a state with a Toss Up governor race.

upcoming.title: Arizona in-person early voting ends
upcoming.what: Arizona's in-person early voting closes Friday; emergency voting runs through Monday and mail ballots must be returned by 7 p.m. Election Day.
upcoming.why: Arizona's early ballots are running R+0.9 by registration with the Hobbs-Biggs governor race on the ballot.

upcoming.title: South Carolina early voting ends
upcoming.what: South Carolina's two-week early-voting period closes Saturday.
upcoming.why: The Graham-Andrews Senate race tied in the Times/Siena poll is the Democrats' outside shot at a sixth pickup.

upcoming.title: North Carolina early voting ends
upcoming.what: One-stop early voting closes at 3 p.m.; Michael Bitzer projects a little under 3 million early ballots, against 2.1 million in 2022.
upcoming.why: How much of the Democratic early-vote surge is new turnout rather than shifted Election Day voters shows in the final count.

upcoming.title: Michigan early in-person voting ends
upcoming.what: The statewide nine-day early-voting period that opened Oct 24 ends Nov 1.
upcoming.why: Michigan's Senate race is the closest of the Democratic-leaning seats, and its early vote has no party registration to read.
upcoming.src: Bridge Michigan voter guide, accessed Oct 26

upcoming.title: Wisconsin and Ohio early in-person voting ends
upcoming.what: In-person absentee voting in Wisconsin and early in-person voting in Ohio close Sunday Nov 1.
upcoming.why: Wisconsin's governor race and Ohio's Senate and governor races are among the closest on the map; Ohio's early vote has run Democratic by last primary ballot.

upcoming.title: Nebraska in-person early voting ends
upcoming.what: Nebraska's in-person early voting at county election offices ends the day before Election Day.
upcoming.why: Last early ballots in the Osborn-Ricketts Senate race and the governor race.
upcoming.src: Civic Nebraska election calendar, accessed Oct 27

upcoming.title: Iowa, Kansas and Minnesota early voting ends
upcoming.what: In-person early voting closes Monday Nov 2 in Iowa, Kansas and Minnesota.
upcoming.why: Iowa and Kansas hold the two Senate races the prediction markets rate closest (47% and 46% Democratic), plus Toss Up governor races.

upcoming.title: Nevada polls close; Alaska follows after midnight ET
upcoming.what: Polls close at 10 p.m. ET in Nevada and Montana; most of Alaska closes at midnight ET and the Aleutian Islands at 1 a.m. ET on Nov. 4.
upcoming.why: Alaska's Senate race, rated a Toss-up by Inside Elections, is likely to be among the last competitive contests to report.

upcoming.title: First polls close in Indiana and Kentucky
upcoming.what: Polls in the Eastern time portions of Indiana and Kentucky close at 6 p.m. ET, with the rest of both states closing at 7 p.m. ET.
upcoming.why: The first returns of the night include House races such as KY-06, which Inside Elections moved to Lean Republican.

upcoming.title: Polls close in Georgia, South Carolina, Virginia, most of Florida
upcoming.what: Polls close at 7 p.m. ET in Georgia, South Carolina, Virginia and Vermont, in most of Florida (the western Panhandle at 8 p.m. ET) and at most New Hampshire polling places (all by 8 p.m. ET).
upcoming.why: First returns arrive in the Georgia, South Carolina, Florida and New Hampshire Senate races and the Georgia and Florida governor races.

upcoming.title: Polls close in North Carolina and Ohio
upcoming.what: Polls close at 7:30 p.m. ET in North Carolina, Ohio and West Virginia.
upcoming.why: Results begin in the North Carolina and Ohio Senate races and the Ohio governor race.

upcoming.title: Polls close in Maine, Pennsylvania, most of Michigan, Texas
upcoming.what: Polls close at 8 p.m. ET in Maine, Pennsylvania and the rest of New Hampshire, and in most of Michigan, Texas and Kansas, whose westernmost areas close at 9 p.m. ET.
upcoming.why: First results arrive in the Maine, Michigan, Texas and Kansas Senate races and the Michigan and Texas governor races.

upcoming.title: Polls close in Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, Wisconsin, Arizona
upcoming.what: Polls close at 9 p.m. ET in Iowa, Minnesota, Nebraska, Wisconsin and Arizona.
upcoming.why: Results begin in the Iowa, Minnesota and Nebraska Senate races and the Iowa, Wisconsin and Arizona governor races.
